definition: why one scale from high to low cannot hold a profile shaped like mine

settled:
One scale is the wrong shape for me. There is no single point between high and low that I sit at.

Some of it has very high ceilings: thinking in conceptual systems, twelve-hour days of focused attention on something I am interested in, perfect scores in linear algebra.

Other parts have floors near zero: working memory at about half of normal, company that has to be accounted for by the minute, and a burnout that took my nervous system down to one percent.

High-functioning actively misleads. It reads off the ceilings anyone can see and denies the floors that are doing the actual disabling.

title: Why High-Functioning Is The Wrong Word
